pos.personaBrief: No verified possession evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge, Allegri's Juventus kept the ball patiently against Serie A low blocks but happily ceded it in big European games and countered, consistent with the verified 'sit back after early ascendency' and result-first 'corto muso' stance.

pro.personaBrief: Khel Now notes 84% short passes on the ground and a 3-2-5 attacking shape, so the team built patiently, but Allegri was pragmatic and readily used long balls (Bonucci to Mandzukic/Higuain) when the forward was free or the press high.

est.personaBrief: Allegri searched for 'the most suitable system for his players' and planned to give Dybala and Pjanic more freedom (Calciomercato 2016), favouring player-driven, fluid roles over fixed zones, with forwards dropping to combine.

lar.personaBrief: Width is a gap; from general knowledge, the verified 3-5-2 and 4-3-1-2 shapes relied on central midfielders and wing-backs rather than touchline wingers, while width came from Alex Sandro/Lichtsteiner crossing to Mandzukic, so a mixed profile.

blo.personaBrief: Verified 5-3-2 defensive shape (Khel Now) and switching to 3-5-2 late to protect results (Wikipedia), plus the preview of sitting back after an early lead, point to a compact mid-to-low block rather than high pressing.

mar.personaBrief: Marking is not directly verified; the compact 5-3-2/4-4-2 blocks described imply zonal defending of spaces, with no evidence of dedicated man-markers on stars.

pla.personaBrief: Allegri inherited Conte's 3-5-2, then rotated 4-3-1-2/4-4-2/4-3-3 and adopted 4-2-3-1 mainly for Europe, adapting systems to players and opponents and changing shape in-game to protect results (Wikipedia, Calciomercato).

res.personaBrief: The stated 'corto muso' line ('who loses by a short nose is second, who wins like that is first') and the 3-5-2 switch in the last 20 minutes to protect results make this a clear result-first profile.

sis.personaBrief: Allegri fitted systems around his players and planned freedom with fewer defensive duties for Dybala and Pjanic (Calciomercato 2016), trusting talent to decide games over a rigid system.

jog.personaBrief: Player type is a gap; from general knowledge, Allegri prized technical quality (Pjanic as regista, Dybala as free 10) and was sceptical of physical-intensity dogma, though the squad was also robust physically (Khedira, Mandzukic).

bas.personaBrief: Verified: the 2019 Juve squad was eight years older than Ajax's, with several players in their 30s by 2018; the club bought finished products and Allegri leaned on veterans for titles.

lid.personaBrief: Allegri managed a rotating squad, stressing the value of fringe players (2016 bench quote) and a calm group atmosphere, while still asserting his authority over stars when needed.
